object_context: For a non-trivial A subset Gamma with U=A^c, non-empty generator family B, and one shared integral family Lambda={(H_i,E_i)}_{i=1}^t that covers every semi-filter above A in the sense of Cavalar-Oliveira Definition 21, freeze the pre-candidate search interface for a source-native property of the shared t-pair cyclic/cover system whose value is universally bounded as a proved function of t and remains informative after cheap-target and multiplexing controls. No property, score, invariant, graph target, lemma, or proof candidate is selected here.
structural_coordinates: Object/QoI: the object is the integral cover witness (Gamma,A,B,U,Lambda) and its shared incidence/rule system; the QoI is whether a future source-native quantity can be universally upper-bounded from t=|Lambda| strongly enough to support a lower bound on rho(A,B).
Definition 21 quantifies over one common integral pair family Lambda that must cover every semi-filter over U that is above some a in A; pair resources may be reused across many obligations.
The cover graph Phi_{A,B} is a set-cover/dominating-set representation: pair vertices are candidate resources and semi-filter vertices are obligations; rho(A,B) is the minimum integral cover size.
Theorem 30 gives the exact identity rho(A,B)=D_cyclic_intersection(A|B); a t-pair universal bound is therefore the root-facing coordinate, whereas an evaluation-only statistic has no authority.

Theorem 24 equations (6)-(8) encode the fixed-Lambda construction by base generator incidence, pair antecedent/intersection incidence, and inclusion relations; its propagation terminates by t+1 stages.

For fixed Lambda, the later pointwise closure trajectory factors through the full base incidence state and shared rule/inclusion system; later stages do not independently distinguish equal base states.

Theorem 37 uses the inclusion/incidence description of a t-pair system, for fixed graph-generator family G_{N,N}, to encode the generated target in O(t(|B|+t)) bits and obtain rho=Theta(N) for random graphs.

Any retained future route must preserve integrality, shared-rule reuse, noncanonical full-semi-filter obligations, and exact model legality; fractional, canonical-only, scalar-only, and repeated-gadget projections have registered failures.

Cheap-target control is blocking: a quantity that is large on a family with a proved O(log N) or polylogarithmic unrestricted construction cannot yield the desired universal super-logarithmic lower bound there.

equivalent_formulations: Integral cover graph: select t pair vertices whose neighborhoods cover all above-A semi-filter vertices.
Cyclic discrete complexity: by Theorem 30 the same optimum equals the minimum number of fan-in-two intersection operations in a convergent cyclic syntactic sequence generating A from B.

Shared rule/incidence description: for fixed B, record the inclusion relations among generator traces, pair antecedents and pair intersections that drive equations (6)-(8); Theorem 37 shows this description reconstructs the generated A in its stated scope.

Pointwise monotone closure representation: each witness state evolves under a fixed monotone recurrence, but the fixed-Lambda factorization result makes this a representation of the shared system rather than an independent lower-bound mechanism.

Set-cover dual/packing view: lower bounds may be sought through obligations versus legal integral pair resources, but the plain fractional relaxation is strictly weaker on G_NEQ and cannot be silently substituted for the integral optimum.
solved_analogues: Random bipartite graphs under row/column generators: Cavalar-Oliveira Theorem 37 proves rho(G,G_{N,N})=Theta(N) asymptotically almost surely by a source-native incidence-description/counting argument.
G_NEQ under row/column generators: Cavalar-Oliveira Proposition 40 proves rho_can=rho=D_intersection=log N using canonical semi-filters and normalized separation signatures.
near_solved_analogues: General non-trivial (A,B): Definition 21 and Theorem 30 reduce the root coordinate exactly to integral cover/cyclic intersection size, but do not provide an explicit super-logarithmic family.

Fixed-Lambda Theorem-24 closure: equations (6)-(8) give exact reconstructability from base/shared incidence and an O(t(|B|+t))-scale description in the random-graph proof, but no explicit-target lower bound follows without a separately proved target-side obstruction.

explicit_disanalogies: Random-graph incompressibility is an existence/almost-sure argument and cannot be assigned to a fixed explicit graph without an independent lower bound on the exact encoded object.
Canonical G_NEQ signatures validate joint integral accounting only in the canonical normalization scope; they do not expose full noncanonical semi-filter structure.
The fixed-Lambda closure trajectory is deterministic from the full base state and shared rules, so later-stage entropy, rank, or state counts cannot be treated as newly created hardness.
Fractional set-cover feasibility is not integral shared-family accumulation; the registered G_NEQ gap is unbounded.
Direct-sum or repeated-gadget intuition is unsafe because a common pair system can multiplex across obligations/copies.
Spectral, entropy, rank, or other scalar compression is not source-native lower-bound authority unless a universal t-bound and calibration theorem are separately proved.
Cheap adjacency predicates can compile to cheap unrestricted constructions even when a target appears pseudorandom or algebraically rich.
Horn closure, database dependencies, caching, coding, scheduling, games, and ordinary-life reuse analogies lack an exact authority-preserving map to rho in this atom.

analogy_scan_notes: Mandatory scan boundary covered information theory/coding (succinct rule descriptions), databases and Horn/data-flow closure, engineering caching/shared-resource scheduling, communication games, error-correction, organizational policy reuse, and ordinary team task-sharing. Each supplied only a proposal-level resemblance. Coding lacks an explicit-target incompressibility theorem; Horn/database closure measures evaluation or implication rather than rho; caching/scheduling and team reuse have no proved conservation or per-rule capacity law for legal pair neighborhoods; game/communication mappings were not shown exact for all full semi-filters. Therefore no cross-domain or everyday bridge is retained. The same-domain Theorem-37 encoding and Proposition-40 calibration remain method-transfer rows, not cross-domain authority.
